title: GPU Cloud Deployment Without Leaving Your IDE — Audry Hsu, RunPod
talk_summary: A RunPod product demo of 'Flash', a Python SDK that lets you decorate an async function with an endpoint decorator and have it packaged and deployed to GPU cloud with hot-reload, so you iterate on GPU code from your IDE without commit/Docker-build/registry/GPU-allocation cycles. The rest is vendor positioning (pods vs serverless vs clusters, per-second billing, worker scaling).

takeaways.technique: Decorator-based remote execution with hot reload
takeaways.what_they_do: A local FastAPI dev server runs orchestration code locally while functions marked with an endpoint decorator are packaged and pushed to remote GPU workers on each file change, so the edit-test loop never leaves the IDE.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have hot mod uh file reload. So if you change anything in your application anywhere, then it gets repackaged and pushed up immediately

takeaways.what_they_do: Serverless workers are provisioned on demand and torn down after a configurable idle timeout, so you pay only for request uptime rather than reserved capacity.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we help you auto scale um your workers for you and scale them back down when you don't have any requests happening, so you don't pay for um any idle time
takeaways.numbers: H100 at $0.00116/second; 1 always-on worker + up to 5 max workers in the demo

takeaways.what_they_do: The pipeline/glue code (prompt generation, chaining calls to multiple models) runs locally; only the GPU-bound function is shipped to the cloud. This keeps orchestration cheap and fast while offloading only the expensive step.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Everything around it, your um main function, any helper functions that you have, those all run on your local development environment, but if you need GPU compute, that that can run um on the cloud
